time.desc: One party’s civil reputation/infringement dispute was confirmed to have entered the second instance procedure and has been accepted by the superior court.

A blogger published an article supporting the accuser, which received a large number of reposts within a few hours and was blocked by the platform. The author claimed that he was reported and attacked by an organized organization.
Several high school alumni of the accused party showed their identity documents to reporters, confirming that they had a history of misconduct in their early years.

A large number of accounts with the name "Brothers Helping Each Other" have emerged on social platforms to teach men strategies for dealing with sexual harassment accusations, and some promote violent confrontation.
The thesis of the party involved was removed from the public academic resource platform, raising concerns about the retraction process and the school’s involvement.

Previous articles published by the tutor of the accused girl have also been withdrawn. His dissertation involved in the incident has been downloaded approximately 300,000 times but has zero citations.
The second instance of the civil dispute made a final judgment and upheld the original judgment. All the plaintiff’s claims were ultimately not supported.

The accused boy has filed an appeal after losing the first instance of an administrative lawsuit against the school regarding demerit penalties. As of this stage, the final result has not been made public.
The university involved had a major personnel change before and after the judicial outcome. The original party committee secretary resigned and was replaced by someone else.

The school issued a review notice: revoking the school disciplinary sanctions against the accused party, determining that the accusation was not judicially supported, and at the same time initiating accountability for relevant personnel and maintaining the other party's degree.

In the review report, the school announced accountability measures for the relevant responsible persons, including suspending the enrollment qualifications of the tutors involved for two years and giving intra-party warnings or admonitions to relevant managers.
In the review report, the school clarified that the online rumor that "the woman's relative holds a senior position in the school" is not true.

The school once again issued a notice upholding the result of "cancelling the demerit penalty for boys and maintaining the master's degree for girls." This "50-point ban for each" has triggered questions on social platforms about "zero cost of false accusation" and negative evaluation of the school's credibility.

For the first time, the university involved officially refuted many online rumors, including that the accuser's paper was rated as excellent, that the accused interrupted his studies due to cyber violence, and that his elder died or became a vegetative state. These rumors are all untrue.
In the review report, the university involved pointed out problems such as lax supervision by instructors and omissions in the college’s review.

The university involved announced a review and formed an investigation team of five experts, investigated more than 20 people and reviewed nearly 100 documents, and finally determined that the accuser's dissertation was not plagiarized and his degree was not revoked.
The parties involved in the incident spoke out intensively on social platforms to confront others and defend themselves, triggering a new round of online controversy.
The accuser posted multiple self-defense posts on social media accounts and had intense confrontations with others, which was described by followers as a "death struggle."
